title: Black Friday GPU Deals 2026: What a Good Price Looks Like
h1: Black Friday GPU Deals 2026: What a Good Price Is per Card
description: A good Black Friday 2026 GPU price is below the card's usual street band: RTX 5070 under $560, RX 9070 XT under $620. Price targets for 16 cards, Nov 27.
dek: Black Friday is Friday, November 27, 2026, and Cyber Monday is November 30. Here is the price at which each current graphics card becomes a real deal, and the traps to skip.
quickAnswer: A real Black Friday GPU deal is a price below the low end of the card's usual street band. Good targets for 2026: RX 9060 XT 16GB at $350 or less, RTX 5060 Ti 16GB at $430 or less, RX 9070 at $550 or less, RTX 5070 at $560 or less, RX 9070 XT at $620 or less, RTX 5070 Ti at $780 or less and RTX 5080 at $1,050 or less.
intro: This page will not list live deals: they change by the hour. Instead it gives a price target for each of the 16 graphics cards we track, based on the card's launch price and its usual US street price band, so you can tell a real Black Friday deal from a markdown of an inflated list price.

A good price is at or below the low end of the card's normal band. A great price is below the launch price or clearly under the band. The targets are our own guidance from those bands, not quotes from any retailer.

sections.h: What Is a Good Black Friday Price for Each GPU?
body: Use the table below as a checklist on Black Friday and Cyber Monday. If a card is at or under the Good column from a reputable seller, it is a fair buy. If it reaches the Great column, buy it if it is the card you wanted anyway. A price above the street band is not a deal, whatever the crossed-out price says.
Partner models with large coolers usually sit $30 to $100 above these targets. That premium can be worth it for a quieter card, but compare it with the base model at the same retailer first.

sections.h: Which GPUs Are Worth Buying on Black Friday 2026?
body: For 1080p, the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/) is the card to watch. At $350 or less it is the best-value card on this list, with 16 GB of memory that keeps it useful for years. The [RTX 5060 Ti 16GB](/gear/rtx-5060-ti-16gb/) is the NVIDIA choice at $430 or less.

For 1440p, watch the [RX 9070](/gear/rx-9070/) and [RX 9070 XT](/gear/rx-9070-xt/). An RX 9070 at $550 or less, with 16 GB, is a stronger long-term buy than a 12 GB [RTX 5070](/gear/rtx-5070/) at the same price, unless you want DLSS 4 and NVENC. Our [RTX 5070 vs RX 9070 XT](/compare/rtx-5070-vs-rx-9070-xt/) comparison covers that choice.

For 4K, the [RTX 5070 Ti](/gear/rtx-5070-ti/) under $780 is the best-value high-end card. The [RTX 5080](/gear/rtx-5080/) is worth it at or near $999; above about $1,150 the 5070 Ti is the better buy.

sections.h: Which GPU Deals Should You Skip?
body: Some discounts look large but buy a card that is a poor choice at any price close to its band. Skip these unless the price is far below the Great column.
list: 8 GB cards for new AAA games: the RTX 5060, RTX 5060 Ti 8GB and RX 9060 XT 8GB run out of memory in more new releases. A $50 to $80 step to a 16 GB model is usually worth it.
The RTX 4060 near $280 to $300: the RTX 5060 costs about the same and is newer. The 4060 makes sense only well under $260.
The RTX 4070 near $550: the RTX 5070 and RX 9070 cost about the same with newer features or more memory.
Bundles that add software or accessories you would not buy, priced above the card's band.
Cards from unknown marketplace sellers far below every other listing. If it looks too cheap, check the seller and return policy first.

sections.h: How Do You Tell a Real GPU Deal From a Fake One?
body: Ignore the crossed-out price. Retailers often show a list price that the card rarely sold for, which makes any markdown look large. Compare the sale price with the card's usual street band in the table above, and with the price history on a tracker such as PCPartPicker or camelcamelcamel for Amazon listings.

Check the exact model name. Many cards share a name across memory sizes, such as the RX 9060 XT 8GB and 16GB, or the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB and 16GB. A deal headline that leaves out the memory size usually means the cheaper 8 GB version. Also confirm the seller: a listing sold and shipped by the retailer itself is safer than a third-party seller on the same site.

sections.h: Should You Buy a GPU on Black Friday or Wait for Cyber Monday?
body: If a card you want hits the Great column on Black Friday, buy it. Prices on popular cards often do not fall further on Cyber Monday, and stock at the lowest price can run out. If it is only at the Good column, waiting until Cyber Monday on November 30 is reasonable, as long as you accept the risk of missing it.

Many large US retailers extend their return windows for holiday purchases into January. Check the policy at checkout. An extended window means you can buy at a good price now and still return the card if a better deal appears or the card has a problem.

sections.h: Is a Prebuilt Gaming PC a Better Black Friday Deal Than a GPU?
body: Sometimes, if you need a whole PC. Prebuilt systems are often discounted on Black Friday, and the discount can cover Windows and assembly. Price the parts first: check the GPU against the table here and the rest against our [how much does a gaming PC cost](/how-much-does-a-gaming-pc-cost/) breakdown.

Look past the graphics card in a prebuilt. Budget power supplies, single-channel memory and small SSDs are common ways to cut cost. Our [best prebuilt gaming PC](/best-prebuilt-gaming-pc/) guide lists what to check.

sections.h: Do You Need a New Power Supply for a Black Friday GPU?
body: Check before you buy, because a cheap card that needs a new power supply is not a cheap upgrade. The RX 9060 XT 16GB and RTX 5060 Ti 16GB run on a good 550 W unit. The RX 9070 and RTX 5070 call for 650 W, the RX 9070 XT and RTX 5070 Ti for 750 W, the RTX 5080 for 850 W and the RTX 5090 for 1,000 W, according to their makers.

Power supplies are discounted on Black Friday too, so if you need one, buy both together. Run your system through the [PSU calculator](/tools/psu-calculator/) and see our [power supply guide](/best-power-supply/) for options.

sections.h: Will GPU Prices Drop After Black Friday?
body: Nobody can promise that. Memory prices rose through 2025 and 2026, which has kept many 16 GB cards at or above launch price for long stretches, so a dip to the low end of a band is not guaranteed to come back soon. If the card you want reaches a Good target from a reliable seller, it is a reasonable time to buy.
If your current card still runs your games well, there is no pressure. Know the target price for the card you want and buy when it gets there, on Black Friday or any other week.

mistakes: The original price shown in a sale is often a list price the card rarely sold at. Compare against the usual street band instead, and check a price tracker for the last few months.
Missing the memory size in the listing
The RX 9060 XT and RTX 5060 Ti come in 8 GB and 16 GB versions with the same name. A headline deal that omits the memory size is usually the 8 GB card.
Buying more card than your CPU can use
A Black Friday RTX 5080 on an older six-core CPU spends much of its time waiting. Check the pair in the bottleneck calculator before buying up a tier.
A $550 card that also needs a $120 power supply is a $670 upgrade. Check the maker's PSU recommendation and your current unit before checking out.
Third-party listings far below every other price are a common source of returns trouble. Prefer cards sold and shipped by the retailer, and check the return policy.
bottomLine: A real Black Friday GPU deal is a price below the card's usual street band, not a big discount from an inflated list price. In 2026 the targets to watch are the RX 9060 XT 16GB at $350 or less, the RX 9070 at $550 or less, the RX 9070 XT at $620 or less, the RTX 5070 at $560 or less and the RTX 5070 Ti at $780 or less. Check the memory size, the seller and your power supply before you buy.

faqs.a: Black Friday 2026 is Friday, November 27, and Cyber Monday is Monday, November 30. Many retailers start deals earlier in the week and run some through the following weekend.

faqs.q: What is a good Black Friday price for an RTX 5070?
faqs.a: $560 or less is a good price for an RTX 5070, and $520 or less is a great one. It launched at $549 and usually sells for $550 to $650. At the same price, compare it with the RX 9070, which has 16 GB of memory.

faqs.q: What is a good Black Friday price for an RX 9070 XT?
faqs.a: $620 or less is a good price for an RX 9070 XT, and $580 or less is a great one. It launched at $599 and usually sells for $600 to $730. It calls for a 750 W power supply.

faqs.q: What is the best GPU deal to look for on Black Friday?
faqs.a: For most people, the RX 9060 XT 16GB at $350 or less for 1080p, or the RX 9070 at $550 or less for 1440p. Both have 16 GB of memory, which keeps them useful longer than 8 GB and 12 GB cards at similar prices.

faqs.q: Are Black Friday GPU deals real?
faqs.a: Some are and some are not. Compare the sale price with the card's usual street band, not the crossed-out price. A price below the low end of the band from a reputable seller is a real deal.

faqs.q: Is it better to buy a GPU on Black Friday or Cyber Monday?
faqs.a: Buy on Black Friday if the card reaches a great price; it may not drop further and stock can run out. If it only reaches a good price, waiting until Cyber Monday on November 30 is reasonable, especially with an extended holiday return window.

faqs.q: Should I buy an 8 GB GPU on Black Friday?
faqs.a: Only for esports and older games, or at a very low price. 8 GB cards run out of memory in more new releases. The 16 GB versions of the RX 9060 XT and RTX 5060 Ti cost about $50 to $80 more and are the safer buy.

faqs.q: Will the RTX 5090 be on sale for Black Friday?
faqs.a: Possibly, but deep discounts are rare. It launched at $1,999 and usually sells for $2,000 to $2,700. Any model at or near $2,100 from a reputable seller is a good price.
